reading.body:
Cyber insurance for AI now spans ten distinct attack classes, from prompt injection to compute hijacking, but the binding theme is that policy language predates the attacks it must cover.

The ten points cluster into three layers: model and data integrity, human and access failures, and physical infrastructure. Prompt injection, model inversion, poisoning, and supply chain malware target the model itself. Shadow AI, biometric spoofing, and API key theft exploit how people use and authenticate to AI systems. Operational technology ransomware, compute hijacking, and act of war exclusions reach building controls and GPU capacity.

For AI scaling, the presence of compute hijacking and operational technology ransomware means underwriters now treat compute and building systems as attack surface, not just data. Stolen GPU workloads and disabled building controls directly reduce available compute, which is the same constraint the broader AI buildout faces. The data does not show loss magnitudes, policy pricing, or which attacks are most frequent, only that insurers have begun naming these exposures.
